newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian 1997 growth estimated at 6.3 pct - bank.
newsitem.headline: Croatian 1997 growth estimated at 6.3 pct - bank.

text.p: Croatia's economy, continuing to recover from the 1991-95 war, could grow at a rate of 6.3 percent in 1997, when inflation should not exceed 5.4 percent, Zagrebacka Banka said in a paper presented on Tuesday.
"The main impulse to growth will come from consumer and investment demand and a favourable impact on exports from economic recovery in Western Europe," said its chief economist Zarko Miljenovic.

Miljenovic, formerly the head of the State Institute of Macroeconomic Analysis and Forecasting, told a news conference his forecast for this year may also be revised up from 4.8 percent to reflect tourism results.

He said it was based on first-half figures, which did not take into account buoyant tourism revenues, which helped related branches in the summer months, and an expected continued dynamic growth till end of the year.
The industrial output, which represents roughly one third of the country's gross domestic product (GDP), was seen as rising 4.4 percent -- considerably less than what government foresees.
For comparison, the government estimates the total 1996 GDP rise at 7-10 percent in real terms and even more nominally.
Miljenovic said nominal GDP could reach 103.4 billion kuna, up from 95.2 billion in 1995.
He put this year's inflation rate at 3.6 percent but said it would accelerate in 1997.
"The year-on-year annual inflation rate of 5.4 percent in 1997 includes a one-off effect of VAT (value added tax). But now we hear it may be posponed so it may be revised," he said.

VAT's introduction at a single rate of 22 percent from the beginning of next year to replace the current turnover tax would increase the price of basic products like food and exacerbate already strained welfare conditions.
It will probably be put off until after the local and presidential elections under pressure from the ruling party HDZ, fearing a loss of votes from the poorest citizens.
